security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline parameter names, and documentation links. I found no prompt-injection attempt or hidden execution logic, but the skill does use a broad infsh CLI permission and sends image prompts or references to an external service.

remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed tools to the specific infsh app run, app sample, and app list commands needed for this skill, if the host supports finer permissions.
Add a clear warning that prompts, generated metadata, and reference image URLs may be processed by inference.sh and the upstream model provider.
Recommend file-based input or structured SDK calls for user-supplied prompts to reduce shell quoting mistakes in long text prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Broad External CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash access to any infsh subcommand with the allowed-tools pattern Bash(infsh *). This is broader than the documented Qwen image workflow and increases impact if prompt guidance is abused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration is explicit, and examples show infsh commands for app sample and app run. The concern is scope expansion, not evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Image Processing Disclosure Needed
semantic_findings.description: The skill sends prompts and reference image locations to inference.sh for remote image generation. Users may expose confidential text, image URLs, or creative assets unless the skill warns them clearly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill states that it uses inference.sh and includes reference image URI inputs. This confirms external processing, but it appears to be disclosed core functionality rather than covert exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Text-heavy AI images can lose clear lettering and layout detail. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to use Qwen-Image-2.0-Pro for polished images.
actual_capabilities: Runs the inference.sh Qwen-Image-2.0-Pro app for text-to-image generation.
Guides poster, banner, logo, and product image prompts with dimensions.
Supports prompt options for seed, image count, watermark, and negative prompts.
Shows reference image URI workflows for image editing and style transfer.
Provides text rendering tips for quoted copy, font details, and placement.
Includes Python SDK examples for normal and streaming runs.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, authentication, and network access.
Sends prompts and reference image URLs to an external service.
Does not guarantee perfect spelling, hands, faces, or layout in every image.
Must follow documented prompt length, image count, and size constraints.

use_cases.title: Design marketing posters
use_cases.description: Create posters and sale graphics with clear quoted headlines, layout instructions, and controlled dimensions.

use_cases.title: Prepare product visuals
use_cases.description: Generate product photography concepts, campaign images, or banner variations for online stores.

use_cases.title: Edit reference images
use_cases.description: Combine person and outfit references or test style transfer with one to three input images.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Poster
prompt_templates.scenario: A first image request with one clear text element.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use qwen-image-pro to generate one 1024 by 1024 poster. Text: "Grand Opening". Style: clean, modern, blue and white.

prompt_templates.title: Make Banner Variations
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketing request that needs multiple options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate four 1920 by 1080 marketing banner variations for a summer sale. Keep the headline "SUMMER SALE" clear and centered.

prompt_templates.title: Edit With References
prompt_templates.scenario: An image editing workflow with input images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use two reference images. Keep the person from image one, apply the outfit from image two, and return two polished options.

prompt_templates.title: Control Reproducible Text
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced request that needs stable layout and exact copy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 1024 by 1536 event poster with seed 12345, prompt extension disabled, exact quoted title, font placement, and a negative prompt for blurry text.

output_examples.input: Create a launch poster with the headline "New Season" and a clean editorial layout.
output_examples.output: A PNG poster concept with the requested headline, modern layout, and dimensions noted in the result metadata.

output_examples.input: Generate four banner variations for a coffee shop called Bean and Brew.
output_examples.output: Four image options with consistent branding direction, different compositions, and clear headline treatment.

output_examples.input: Use two image references to place an outfit from one image onto the person in another image.
output_examples.output: Two edited PNG options that combine the requested subject and outfit references.

best_practices: Put exact text in quotes and describe placement, font style, size, and color.
Disable prompt extension when precise wording or layout matters.
Avoid sensitive images or confidential text because processing uses an external service.
anti_patterns: Sending private client images without permission or a data handling review.
Combining many unrelated creative directions in one prompt.
Publishing generated text without checking spelling, spacing, and layout.

faq.question: What model does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Alibaba Qwen-Image-2.0-Pro through the inference.sh CLI.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires the infsh CLI to be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents reference image URI inputs for image editing and style transfer workflows.

faq.question: Is text rendering always exact?
faq.answer: No. Quoted text, font details, negative prompts, and disabled prompt extension can improve results.

faq.question: Does it send data to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and reference image URLs are processed through inference.sh and the image model provider.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
